problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the distance between $f(t)=2t$ and the subspace spanned by $g(t)=6t-3$ with respect to the inner product.

activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Inner Product Spaces

feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $2$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the distance between $p(t)=7{t}^{2}-t$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t)=4{t}^{2}-4t$ with respect to the inner product.
feedback.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{q(t)}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1)}{q(-1)q(-1)+q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1)}\cdot q(t) \\  & =\frac{{\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(7{t}^{2}-t){|}_{t=i}\cdot (4{t}^{2}-4t){|}_{t=i}}{{\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(4{t}^{2}-4t){|}_{t=i}\cdot (4{t}^{2}-4t){|}_{t=i}}\cdot (4{t}^{2}-4t) \\  & =\frac{8\cdot 8+0\cdot 0+6\cdot 0}{8\cdot 8+0\cdot 0+0\cdot 0}\cdot (4{t}^{2}-4t) \\  & =\frac{64}{64}\cdot (4{t}^{2}-4t) \\  & =4{t}^{2}-4t.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The distance between $p(t)=7{t}^{2}-t$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t)=4{t}^{2}-4t$ with respect to our inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖p(t)-{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t)‖ \\  & =‖7{t}^{2}-t-(4{t}^{2}-4t)‖ \\  & =‖3{t}^{2}+3t‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨3{t}^{2}+3t,3{t}^{2}+3t⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨3{t}^{2}+3t,3{t}^{2}+3t⟩ & ={\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(3{t}^{2}+3t){|}_{t=i}\cdot (3{t}^{2}+3t){|}_{t=i} \\  & =0\cdot 0+0\cdot 0+6\cdot 6 \\  & =0+0+36 \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d=\sqrt{36}=6.$
